title: Apply the Zvec/Qdrant swap, consolidate all tool-adoption research into one registry, and add a PostToolUse reminder hook to keep it updated
objective: Owner-directed: (1) apply the Zvec-over-Qdrant preference (and TurboVec as a narrower alternative) discussed this session into docs/research/architecture-studio-open-source-options.md's Deferred candidates table; (2) create docs/research/RESEARCH-DECISIONS-REGISTRY.md, a single consolidated index over every candidate evaluated across both existing research docs, categorized by status (Adopted / Standby-deferred / Discarded / Reference-only) so decisions, discards, and standby items are visible in one place instead of scattered across documents; (3) add a lightweight, advisory (never-blocking) PostToolUse hook -- verified against the real Claude Code hooks spec via WebFetch on code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md before writing, not guessed -- that fires when a Write/Edit touches a docs/research/*.md file other than the registry itself, injecting an additionalContext reminder to also update the registry. The provider-neutral logic lives in tools/scripts/research-registry-reminder.mjs (reusing normalizeRepositoryPath from agent-task-guard.mjs), wired via a thin .claude/settings.json adapter, mirroring the existing agent-task-guard.mjs pattern; also cross-referenced into .ai/coordination/PROTOCOL.md and AGENTS.md as a provider-neutral rule so Codex/Gemini sessions without the Claude-specific hook still know the convention. AGENTS.md's 'introduce a tool/hook without need and evaluation' and 'changing hooks requires a separate task and explicit owner approval' gates are satisfied by this task record plus the owner's direct, explicit request. Did not search for an existing off-the-shelf OSS tool for this specific need (a Markdown ledger of this repo's own bespoke research docs, wired to this repo's specific hook mechanism) since it is inherently repo-specific bookkeeping with no generic external solution, the same reasoning already applied to why .ai/state/tasks itself is hand-rolled rather than borrowed.
validations: Verified PostToolUse hook mechanics against the real Claude Code docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md) via WebFetch, cross-checking a claude-code-guide subagent's answer rather than trusting it alone: confirmed PostToolUse cannot block an already-run tool call, confirmed the exact additionalContext JSON shape ({hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName,additionalContext}}), and confirmed matcher filters by tool name only (chose to filter by path inside the script itself, matching agent-task-guard.mjs's existing style, rather than relying on the less-certain settings.json 'if' glob syntax).

Applied the Zvec/TurboVec-over-Qdrant preference to docs/research/architecture-studio-open-source-options.md's Deferred candidates table, keeping the same admission condition (Tantivy plus graph queries must first prove insufficient).

Created docs/research/RESEARCH-DECISIONS-REGISTRY.md consolidating every candidate from both existing research documents (~55 entries) under a 4-state status legend (Adopted/Standby/Discarded/Reference-only); confirmed nothing is yet Adopted, which is accurate, not a gap.

tools/scripts/research-registry-reminder.mjs reuses normalizeRepositoryPath from agent-task-guard.mjs (no duplicated path logic); 7 new unit tests in research-registry-reminder.test.mjs, run together with the existing 16 agent-task-guard tests: node --test tools/scripts/agent-task-guard.test.mjs tools/scripts/research-registry-reminder.test.mjs -- 23/23 pass.

Live end-to-end smoke test of the actual CLI via stdin: confirmed it emits the correct additionalContext JSON for a research-doc edit, and emits nothing (silent, exit 0) both for an edit to the registry itself and for an unrelated file (AGENTS.md).
Wired the hook into .claude/settings.json as a new PostToolUse entry alongside the existing PreToolUse guard entry; validated the file still parses as JSON.

Added the test invocation to .github/workflows/ci.yml next to the existing agent-task-guard.test.mjs line so it runs in CI (ubuntu-latest) -- confirmed the test file uses real mkdtemp-based paths, not hardcoded Windows-style path strings, so it is platform-correct on Linux CI as well as this Windows dev machine.

Cross-referenced the new rule 7 into .ai/coordination/PROTOCOL.md (provider-neutral: the hook is a Claude-specific convenience, the written rule is what Codex/Gemini sessions follow cooperatively) and into AGENTS.md's completion-criteria documentation bullet, mirroring how the existing per-project docs-regen rule and docs-quality-check skill were already cross-referenced.
uv run --package automation python -m automation.coordination --root .: passed, 50 task(s), whole .ai/state/ tree consistent.

Did not spend a research cycle searching for an existing off-the-shelf tool for this specific need: it is bespoke bookkeeping tightly coupled to this repository's own research-doc structure and this repository's own hook mechanism, the same reasoning that already justifies why .ai/state/tasks itself is hand-rolled rather than borrowed.
artifacts: docs/research/architecture-studio-open-source-options.md (Qdrant deferred row split into Qdrant/Zvec/TurboVec, Zvec marked preferred)
risks: Hook is strictly advisory (injects additionalContext only, never blocks/denies) -- verified PostToolUse cannot block a tool call that already ran, per the real Claude Code hooks spec.

The registry is a hand-maintained authored index over other authored research docs, not an auto-generated or model-driven artifact (DEC-035: post-tool maintenance stays deterministic, no model call) -- the hook only reminds, it does not write the registry itself.
No dependency installed, no ADR closed by this task; it only organizes and cross-references research already produced.
